enforcement.tokenBoundary: Checked between assistant turns and before run_code/nested calls; an in-flight provider response cannot be interrupted at an exact token.

common.note: Runtime budgets are enforced by model ID. maxEstimatedSubCalls describes expected work; maxTotalSubCalls is the hard limit with correction headroom. Workload-size fields remain advisory because the extension cannot infer record/shard counts from arbitrary code.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol.rationale: C4 was clean 3/3 and C6 was correct 2/2 with roughly 41k tokens. Most stable PTC model in this benchmark.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra.rationale: C4 was clean 3/3 and C6 was clean 2/2. Occasional path retry was observed below the boundary.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna.rationale: C6 was clean 2/2 after the stdin race fix. Lower levels showed more self-correction and path retries than Sol/Terra.

dashscope/deepseek-v4-flash.rationale: C4 was semantically correct 3/3 historically. Monitored policy runs needed provider/final-formatting time, one extra merge program, and up to nine discovery/re-read calls beyond the 31-call estimate; the 40-call hard cap covers that bounded correction headroom. C5/C6 remained correct but consumed about 1.10M/1.49M tokens, so multi-program complexity is not economical.

dashscope/deepseek-v4-pro.rationale: C4 is the conservative unattended limit. The 120-second wall budget leaves provider/final-formatting headroom without increasing shard, sub-call, or token limits; C5 passed but was slow and expensive, while C6 failed 0/2.
